Exercise: Mountain Climbers

Category:
plyometrics

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- dynamic
- upper_body_assistive
- bilateral
- lower_body_dominant

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- chest
- hamstrings
- shoulders

Equipment:
None

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
high

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: knee injury, reason: high impact and repetitive knee flexion/extension
- condition: shoulder instability, reason: repetitive shoulder abduction and internal rotation

Exercise Variations:

- name: High Knee Mountain Climbers, description: Increase the speed of the leg movements to target higher metabolic demand.
- name: Single-Leg Mountain Climbers, description: Perform the exercise on one leg at a time for enhanced unilateral strength and balance.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Burpees, reason: similar explosive movement pattern and high energy demand

Instructions:

- Begin in a pushup position, with your weight supported by your hands and toes. Flexing the knee and hip, bring one leg until the knee is approximately under the hip. This will be your starting position.
- Explosively reverse the positions of your legs, extending the bent leg until the leg is straight and supported by the toe, and bringing the other foot up with the hip and knee flexed. Repeat in an alternating fashion for 20-30 seconds.
